title: Aquilaria crassna Leaf Extract Ameliorates Glucose-Induced Neurotoxicity In Vitro and Improves Lifespan in Caenorhabditis elegans.
authors: Pattarachotanant, Nattaporn; Sornkaew, Nilubon; Warayanon, Watis; Rangsinth, Panthakarn; Sillapachaiyaporn, Chanin; Vongthip, Wudtipong; Chuchawankul, Siriporn; Prasansuklab, Anchalee; Tencomnao, Tewin
one_liner_zh: 研究植物提取物对高糖诱导神经毒性的保护作用，仅含分子对接但非蛋白-DNA互作，与本课题无关。
abstract: Hyperglycemia is one of the important causes of neurodegenerative disorders and aging. Aquilaria crassna Pierre ex Lec (AC) has been widely used to relieve various health ailments. However, the neuroprotective and anti-aging effects against high glucose induction have not been investigated. This study aimed to investigate the effects of hexane extract of AC leaves (ACH) in vitro using human neuroblastoma SH-SY5Y cells and in vivo using nematode Caenorhabditis elegans. SH-SY5Y cells and C. elegans were pre-exposed with high glucose, followed by ACH treatment. To investigate neuroprotective activities, neurite outgrowth and cell cycle progression were determined in SH-SY5Y cells. In addition, C. elegans was used to determine ACH effects on antioxidant activity, longevity, and healthspan. In addition, ACH phytochemicals were analyzed and the possible active compounds were identified using a molecular docking study. ACH exerted neuroprotective effects by inducing neurite outgrowth via upregulating growth-associated protein 43 and teneurin-4 expression and normalizing cell cycle progression through the regulation of cyclin D1 and SIRT1 expression. Furthermore, ACH prolonged lifespan, improved body size, body length, and brood size, and reduced intracellular ROS accumulation in high glucose-induced C. elegans via the activation of gene expression in the DAF-16/FoxO pathway. Finally, phytochemicals of ACH were analyzed and revealed that beta-sitosterol and stigmasterol were the possible active constituents in inhibiting insulin-like growth factor 1 receptor (IGFR). The results of this study establish ACH as an alternative medicine to defend against high glucose effects on neurotoxicity and aging.
abstract_zh: 高血糖是神经退行性疾病和衰老的重要原因之一。沉香（Aquilaria crassna Pierre ex Lec, AC）已被广泛用于缓解多种健康问题。然而，其针对高糖诱导的神经保护和抗衰老作用尚未被研究。本研究旨在使用人神经母细胞瘤SH-SY5Y细胞进行体外实验，并使用线虫（Caenorhabditis elegans）进行体内实验，探讨AC叶片己烷提取物（ACH）的作用。SH-SY5Y细胞和线虫预先暴露于高糖环境，随后进行ACH处理。为研究神经保护活性，测定了SH-SY5Y细胞中的神经突生长和细胞周期进程。此外，使用线虫评估ACH对抗氧化活性、寿命和健康寿命的影响。同时，分析了ACH的植物化学成分，并通过分子对接研究鉴定了可能的活性化合物。ACH通过上调生长相关蛋白43和teneurin-4表达诱导神经突生长，并通过调节cyclin D1和SIRT1表达使细胞周期进程正常化，从而发挥神经保护作用。此外，ACH延长了高糖诱导线虫的寿命，改善了体型、体长和产卵量，并通过激活DAF-16/FoxO通路中的基因表达减少了细胞内ROS积累。最后，对ACH的植物化学成分分析显示，β-谷甾醇和豆甾醇是抑制胰岛素样生长因子1受体（IGFR）的可能活性成分。本研究结果确立了ACH作为对抗高糖诱导的神经毒性和衰老效应的替代药物。
